statements.text: Americans cannot pick up a newspaper without a near daily reminder that artificial intelligence, or AI, is transforming the world as we know it. With a few keystrokes, a layperson can generate an image indistinguishable from a photograph and can make a business plan based on AI-driven, supply chain predictive analysis, or write code for a new application.
statements.venue: House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing, IP and Strategic Competition with China Part III: IP Theft, Cybersecurity, and AI, opening statement

statements.text: 🧵(3/3) Of the leading nations on AI, the U.S. stands out for its absence of basic rules of the road. Many have called on the U.S. Government to regulate AI and I was eager to hear from our witnesses on this important issue. https://t.co/h7ehfsGZTi

AI cannot be listed as an inventor on a patent. It cannot own a copyright. The courts and the Copyright Office have, respectively, already addressed those basic questions. The question of how much AI involvement renders a product as no longer having been created by a human being remains open.
statements.venue: House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing, AI and IP Part III: IP protection for AI-assisted inventions and creative works, opening statement

statements.text: Because of these technological advancements, 2024 will be the first AI Presidential election, where deep fake and misinformation will have the power to deceive voters, making an abnormally consequential election even more consequential and controversial. Abuse of women through the creation of explicit images with generative AI is already a problem, and if you don't believe me, ask Taylor Swift about that.
statements.venue: House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing, AI and IP Part II: Identity in the Age of AI (Los Angeles), opening statement

statements.text: Our question today is not if, but how, Congress should act to protect artists from such treatment. It is our responsibility as legislators to ensure that the creators who enrich our society with their talent and work are able to live and thrive in the age of AI.
statements.venue: House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing, AI and IP Part II: Identity in the Age of AI (Los Angeles), opening statement

statements.text: The main ingredient for artificial intelligence is data, which allows AI models to learn. Co-President Musk owns an AI company with its Chatbot Grock, and there is always the problem of AI companies needing to get a competitive edge to have more data to train their models, and Co President Musk is in a unique position now, because he also runs the so-called Department of Government Efficiency—DOGE.
statements.venue: House hearing statement on DOGE data access and AI training

statements.quoted: There are so many reasons I'm voting "no" on the Big, Ugly Bill. The devastating effects on Georgians include cuts to Medicaid and Affordable Care Act coverage. In Georgia alone, 530,600 people will lose Affordable Care Act tax credits and 93,429 will lose Medicaid coverage.

statements.text: When you preempt an entire field of law, you’re preempting the common law right along with it. [...] By protecting common law, we can protect that floor that ensures every person harmed can seek to have their case heard before a court of law. This basic standard of care can spur innovation by preventing a race to the bottom, and it can offer a level of security as the federal government and states determine what the best next steps are for AI in the United States.
statements.venue: House Judiciary IP/AI Subcommittee hearing on federal preemption of state AI laws, opening statement (press release)

statements.text: Common law cases to protect consumers are already being filed against generative AI platforms. Two days ago, Senator Hawley held a hearing on the harms to children using AI technology, calling witnesses whose children died or were hospitalized after interacting with artificial intelligence chatbots.
statements.venue: House Judiciary IP/AI Subcommittee hearing on federal preemption of state AI laws, opening statement (press release)

statements.text: Across creative industries, innovators from writers and software developers to musicians and painters, are watching their works used to train AI models for free while the barrier to entry gets higher and higher. [...] This means acknowledging creators as a key part of the ecosystem that is building AI and compensating them as such. This means enacting protections for American workers, building responsibly, and deploying equitably.
statements.venue: House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing, A Midlife Crisis? IP and the Internet After 40, opening statement

statements.text: Data centers are driving up utility costs, straining the grid and degrading the quality of the everyday appliances families depend on, like our air conditioning and heating system.
